article.title: Effects of Milk or Yogurt Supplementation on Bone Health, Body Composition, and Gut Microbiota in Canadian Young Adults: Protocol for a Three-Arm Parallel-Group Randomized Controlled Trial.
article.authors: Uzair SA, Monroy-Valle M, Shafiee M
article.abstract: Osteoporosis is a major global public health concern. Optimizing peak bone mass during young adulthood is the main preventive strategy for reducing fracture risk later in life. Dairy foods, such as milk, provide nutrients, including calcium and protein, that support bone health, while fermented dairy foods, including yogurt, may confer additional benefits through potential modulation of the gut microbiome. However, the long-term comparative effects of milk and/or yogurt supplementation compared with no dairy supplementation on bone health, body composition, and the gut microbiome in Canadian young adults remain unknown.
